unequip.tooltip: This includes weapons, armour, cyberware and your arms.

shop.bSellConsumeTooltip: Sell all alcohol, drinks and food.
shop.bSellSelectedTooltip: You need to select the type of item you want to sell.
shop.bDisaSelectedTooltip: You need to select a type of item you want to disassemble.
shop.bSellGrenadeTooltip: Sell all grenades regardless of quality.
shop.converttooltip:
Either select a type you want to keep
or leave it empty and the script will
default to Water and Cat Food.

equipment.tModUpgr:
Upgrade quality of mods and scopes in your backpack
that naturally come in random qualities.
equipment.tUpgradeAll1: This will attempt to force EVERYTHING in your inventory to the selected tier.
equipment.tUpgradeAll2: Use WITH CAUTION, and AT YOUR OWN RISK - not all items tolerate being forced to all tiers.
equipment.tUpgradeAll3: You will need to save/load after running this, in order for the inventory screen to correctly update.
equipment.tEquipQual:
Only required if you chose 'Level and Quality'
or 'Quality Only' mode.

questtag.tooltip:
Equip items that have the quest flag like Johnny's
clothing, leave the inventory and hit this button.

weaponMods.tBeastMode: 100% Block strength, +200% Stamina cost reduction, better dismemberment chance for blades, combo infinitely.
weaponMods.tSuperZoom: Enables more zoom when aiming down sights
weaponMods.tPenetrator: 100% Armor Penetration, all ranged weapons gain cover "pierce" ability like fully charged Tech Weapons.
weaponMods.tBigBrain: Smart weapons get a huge aiming area, many more targets, faster lock, faster projectiles, perfect accuracy and massive lock range. Combine with Psycho Mode for truly awesome amounts of carnage :D
weaponMods.tBigBrain2: Fair warning however: Combined with Psycho Mode, there's so much physics calculation that needs to be done when you shoot, that it can get a bit laggy!
weaponMods.tPsychoMode: Super fast firing, more projectiles per shot
weaponMods.tSuperAcc: Weapons will have very little bullet spread.

ammo.tAutoInv:
Automatically refill inventory ammo pool of currently
equipped weapon. Weapon still needs to be reloaded.
ammo.tAutoMag:
Automatically refill magazine ammo pool of currently
equipped weapon. Weapon doesn't need to be reloaded.
ammo.tManual: Refill Handgun, Rifle, Shotgun and Sniper Rifle ammo.

additems.tForceQual: Use this to force item quality, at your own risk. Not all items are available in all qualities.
additems.tItemAll: Adds specified amount of every item in the category.
additems.tForceQual2: Safest with items listed as "Random" quality in the list above. Generally only applies to weapons, clothing and (some) cyberware.
additems.tForceQual3: By default, "Random" items are automatically scaled to your level.

perks.tRes: Reset All Perks and refund all points.
perks.tAddAll: Adds all perks without spending your current perk points.
perks.tRem: Remove the perk selected above - points will be refunded.
perks.tAddRelicPoint: NOTE: This won't work if you don't have Phantom Liberty installed.

stats.tooltip: Temporary, gets reset upon reloading a save or restarting the game.
stats.pTooltip: This will apply a PERMANENT modifier to your character's stats and CANNOT be removed.
stats.cybCapWarn: Modifying Cyberware Capacity to a value over 400 will cause the Cyberware Capacity graph to disappear in the Cyberware screen.

maxall.tooltip:
Max Player and Street Cred Level (60),
Attributes (20) and Skills (60).

modifiers.tHealItemCooldown: Healing items are available immediately after use.
modifiers.tGrenadeCooldown: Grenades are available immediately after use.
modifiers.tBerserkCooldown: Berserk is available for use immediately after deactivation.
modifiers.tKerenzikovCooldown: Kerenzikov is reusable instantly after triggering.
modifiers.tOverclockCooldown: Cyberdeck Overclock can be reused immediately after deactivation.
modifiers.tQuickhackCooldown: All Quickhacks can be reused immediately.
modifiers.tQuickhackCost: All Quickhacks have the maximum possible cost reduction.
modifiers.tFaceplateCooldown: Behavioral Imprint-Synced Faceplate cyberware can be re-used instantly.
modifiers.tInfJump: Removes the jump limit on double-jump; you can now jump forever. You still need the double-jump cyberlegs, though.
modifiers.tInfAirDash: Air Dash to your heart's content (no longer have to hit the ground to dash again). You still need the Air Dash perk, though.

god.tGod1: Makes you immune to being dead (mostly). Also, prevents most fall damage deaths and landing "splats."
god.tGod2: There are a still number of places with scripted deaths, which cannot be avoided (jumping down the middle of Megabuilding 8, for example).
god.tInvis1: This will make you invisible to enemies, so you will not be spotted/attacked.
god.tInvis2: Attacking an enemy will still make them respond, but they will lose track of you after a little while.

search.tTabName: Search is currently in Alpha, expect some odd edge-cases.
search.headerHint: Right-click the table header to view table column options.
search.tSearchB: You can seach by name, or leave it blank and select a Type/Category. You can also use Type/Category as further filters on a name search.
search.tIconicFilter: Filter out non-iconic items. Applies after Name/Category/Type filters.
search.tTierFilter: Show only items with the selected Tier. Applies after Name/Category/Type filters.
search.tCharWrn: Enter at least 3 letters, or choose a Type/Category.
search.tMaxSlots: Use this to force the item to have the maximum possible mod slots. (Weapons and Clothing only)
search.tSearchAddAll: CAUTION: The more items you add, the longer it'll take to process.

menus.desc:
Items selected below will always stay open.
Each tab has its own sub-menu.

json.desc3: Red entries were modified by you.
json.desc1: Lists misc. variables stored in config.json.
json.desc2: Green means the default value is used.

bigBrain.tReticlePitch: Controls the height of the aiming reticle.
bigBrain.tReticleYaw: Controls the width of the aiming reticle.
bigBrain.tReticlePitchYaw1: These values are in degrees, relative to the field of view, and each other. Setting both to 45 is almost the full screen.
bigBrain.tReticlePitchYaw2: The values influence each other in ways that are difficult to understand. Lowering one increases the effect of the other, and vice versa (even if you don't change it).
bigBrain.tReticlePitchYaw3: Experiment with different values to find a setting that does what you want.

psychoMode.tFireRate1: This applies as a multiplier of the weapon's current fire rate. For semi-automatics, it reduces the delay between trigger pulls.
psychoMode.tFireRate2: Be warned: If you set this too high (particularly if you have lots of additional projectiles) the game WILL crash if the physics system becomes overwhelmed.
psychoMode.tFireRate3: A value of 3 - 5 with 5+ additional projectiles seems relatively stable, but your mileage may vary.

superZoom.tZoomLevel: This applies as a multiplier of the weapon's current zoom level. Set to 1 to disable extra zoom, but still get no sway on ADS.

config.tVersion: This is the version of SM that this mod config is backwards-compatible to.
config.tModVersion: This is the currently installed version of SimpleMenu.
config.tInitNotification: Unchecking this will suppress the "SimpleMenu Initialized Successfully" notification on first load / mod reload.
config.tDebugMode: Checking this will output additional debug information to the console.
config.tLoadingBar: Unchecking this will prevent the loading bar from appearing on first load / mod reload.
config.tLoadingSpeed1: Use this to set the rate at which Items will be indexed for search.
config.tLoadingSpeed2: The higher this value, the faster SimpleMenu will load; too high may cause lag or loading issues - try to find a balance.
config.tEnablePopup: Uncheck this to prevent the hotkey notification popups from appearing.

vehicles.tInstant:
When enabled your owned vehicles appear
right next to you when you call them.
vehicles.tFixCar:
Will repair the Player Vehicle you are looking at. It will respawn.
(Will attempt to do an "instant" spawn, but at worst, it'll be a normal "summon").
vehicles.tInstantRepair: Removes the 5 minute repair timer after a player vehicle explodes. Efficient!

npc_other.tKill: Point at an NPC and hit the button (or hotkey).

breachProto.inMinigame: Options unavailable when Breach Protocol is in progress.
breachProto.tUnsolv1: Allows setting an unsolvable state, e.g. puzzle length larger than buffer length.
breachProto.tUnsolv2: NOTE: It's not guaranteed it'll end up solvable even without this checked, but it should be close. Just be sensible (e.g. don't set the grid to 4x4 with length 10 puzzles)
breachProto.tExceed1: Expands sliders to a larger range of values. This will reset their values to default.
breachProto.tExceed2: This probably won't work the way you think it will, but who am I to deny you the fun?
breachProto.tCustTime: Check this box and set the slider to force all Breach Protocol games to this time limit.
breachProto.tCustGrid: Check this box and set the slider to force all Breach Protocol games to this grid size.
breachProto.tCustBuff: Check this box and set the slider to force Breach Protocol buffer size, regardless of player stats.
breachProto.tCustPuzzLen: Check this box and set the slider to force all Breach Protocol puzzles to this many "bytes".

teleport.tJmpForw: Use this to make a small forward teleport (through a door, wall, etc). Use a negative value to go backwards
teleport.tSaveQt: Sets the Quick Teleport you have selected above as the Saved Location that can be used with the hotkey.
teleport.tSave: Sets your current location as the Saved Location that can be used with the hotkey.
teleport.tCustom: If you can't move after a teleport simply open a menu and close it right after.
teleport.bSaveQt: Set Quick Teleport as Saved Location
teleport.bSave: Set Player Position as Saved Location
teleport.tAddQTel: Save your current location as a new Quick Teleport location
teleport.tRemQTel: Delete the currently selected Quick Teleport location
teleport.tQTelGo: Teleport to currently selected Quick Teleport location

time.tSlowmoself: If you uncheck this, SlowMo won't apply to you
time.tSlowMoEffects:
Choose which SlowMo type you want. "None" avoids a full screen effect, but behaves strangely.
"Sandevistan" and "Kerenzikov" replicate the in-game effects correctly.
time.tSlowMoEffectsNote: NOTE: These effects also include gameplay effects - e.g. the Kerenzikov effect disables dodge/dash, as it is normally triggered by dodge/dash in game.
time.bLockPlayerTiDi: Lock Player to Global Time Dilation
time.freezeTT:
Game keeps running as usual but
time of day won't change anymore.
time.tSlowMoLabelDisabled: Options unavailable while SlowMo is active
time.tDilationSlider: The lower the value, the slower the game.
time.tDilationRatioSlider1: Set the level of time dilation applied to the player, independent of the global value.
time.tDilationRatioSlider2: CTRL + click the slider to manually enter values up to 1000%. The ratio rules still apply. Things will probably get weird - but that's why you're here, right? ;)
time.tDilationRatioSlider3: "Apply to Self" MUST be enabled for this to work. Entering and exiting a game menu will generally reset you back to whatever the global time dilation is. Just toggle on/off to fix.
time.tDilationRatioNote: NOTE: This functions as a ratio of the global time dilation, and cannot exceed 10x. The slider text will change to red and show the maximum speed you can reach when the ratio is exceeded.
time.tScaleCycle1: Attempts to speed up your gun's firing rate to counteract the time dilation. Does okay down to about 50%, then starts to fall behind.
time.tScaleCycle1b: Will generally get further with guns that start off fairly slow firing, but it's ultimately an engine limitation. It is also tied to global dilation, not player, again due to the engine.
time.tScaleCycle2: Does not apply when PSYCHO MODE is enabled.

quest.tUntrack: Requires HUD refresh, hit the ESC key twice, or open the inventory.
quest.tDisable: Sets the selected quest fact to 0, effectively disabling it.
quest.tEnable: Sets the selected quest fact to 1, effectively enabling it.
quest.tEnd: Ends quest and rewards you for completion. Use with caution, preferably only for stuck/broken quests.

police.tHeat: Sets the wanted level to the slider value.
